summary: Long-running model-validation sweep processes crowding dedicated GPUs leading to autoscaler starvation and throughput degradation
description:
Issue summary:
Customer GlacierAI reports recurring midday throughput drops in their dedicated pool starting 2026-03-10. Symptoms include prolonged queue growth, increased p50/p99 latency for batched generation routes, and autoscaler failing to add capacity despite sustained queue depth.

Impact:
- GlacierAI observed ~40% drop in throughput for critical routes during business hours, impacting production SLAs.
- Requests were either queued for >2s or returned 503 when autoscaler failed to attach GPUs quickly.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool: glc-dedicated-us-east-7 (reserved capacity)
- Region: us-east-1
- Time window: recurring 11:30-14:30 UTC on 2026-03-10 through 2026-03-13
- Models: open-llama-13b (primary), redwood-qa-model-v1 (fallback)

Steps to reproduce (customer):
1) Send sustained mix of long-lived validation streams (keep-alive with intermittent tokens, ~2–4 requests/s per stream) across multiple workers used for nightly model-validation sweeps.
2) Observe queue growth on the customer batched route and rising request latency p50->p99.
3) Note autoscaler logs: repeated attach attempts but low attach success rate and no new GPU allocations for several minutes.

Observed logs / metrics / traces:
- Autoscaler metric: attach_success_rate fell from 98% to 62% during the incident window (metrics link: https://metrics.redwood.ai/d/attach/attach_success_rate?org=glacierai).
- Dedicated pool slot occupancy: many slots marked as "in-use" but kernel-level GPU utilization was low (~15–30%) suggesting slot retention with idle GPU time.
- Sidecar logs on several tenant nodes show long-lived grpc streams to model-validation workers with frequent small payloads and occasional checkpoint writes.
- KV cache growth telemetry for open-llama-13b shows prefix cache retention spikes coincident with the sweeps.
- Networking: no packet loss observed, connection latencies normal.

Initial hypothesis:
1) Long-running validation streams are holding slot attachments open while performing intermittent small requests, preventing efficient batch formation and causing slot fragmentation.
2) Background checkpointing from validation workers briefly increases NVMe IO and sidecar CPU, causing attach timeouts and autoscaler to under-react.
3) Autoscaler heuristics treat the retained slots as healthy and thus do not provision additional GPUs quickly enough.

Immediate customer-facing workaround attempted:
- Support recommended pausing the validation sweep during business hours; GlacierAI confirmed throughput recovered when sweeps halted for 30 minutes.
- We put a temporary rule to deprioritize sweep user-agent in routing to non-critical capacity to alleviate customer-facing degradation.

Business impact note:
Customer is on a dedicated contract with SLA expectations for throughput. Recurrent impact risks escalation to account management if sustained.
comments: 2026-03-10 15:10 - Olivia Chen (Support): Customer reports throughput drop and provided sample request IDs and sidecar logs. Asked for pool and node IDs.

2026-03-10 16:05 - Marcus Patel (SRE): Pulled autoscaler attach logs and pool metrics; noticed attach_success_rate drop and many slots marked in-use with low GPU utilization. Created INT-3321 to track internal root-cause analysis.

2026-03-10 17:40 - GlacierAI (Customer): Confirmed that pausing their nightly validation sweep temporarily restored throughput; sweep resumes then degradation returns. Asked for recommended configuration to avoid disruption.

2026-03-11 09:20 - Priya Rao (Serving Runtime Eng): Investigating sidecar checkpointing behavior. Found sidecar thread dumping at checkpoint intervals correlating with short NVMe spikes. Hypothesis: checkpoint writer holds GPU-affiliate locks causing attach latency.

2026-03-12 12:05 - Marcus Patel (SRE): Deployed temporary routing deprioritization for user-agent 'glacier-validate' to best-effort pool; customer routes to critical capacity restored. Monitoring for recurrence.

2026-03-13 14:50 - Engineering Lead (Aaron Weiss): Agreed on two-prong fix: (1) autoscaler heuristic patch to ignore long-held attachments below a CPU/GPU-util threshold, (2) sidecar patch to make checkpoint writer non-blocking with backoff. Assigned follow-up PRs.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-11 - Attach timeline analysis: attach_attempt -> kernel_init -> kvcache_load -> attach_ack. Latency spikes mainly between kernel_init and attach_ack when sidecar IO > 70% for node.
2026-03-11 - Slot audit: ~18% of attachments in pool were from processes with >12h lifespan (validation sweeps), many with <40% GPU utilization during incident windows.

2026-03-12 - Autoscaler review: current heuristic counts attachments as active if slot is held regardless of recent token emission. This hides real available capacity from the autoscaler decision function.
2026-03-12 - KV cache: long-lived streams pinned large prefix states increasing memory pressure and causing background prefetch thrash and occasional small OOMs in helper processes.
resolution:
Mitigation steps applied and next steps:
1) Short-term (applied 2026-03-12): Introduced routing deprioritization for 'glacier-validate' user-agent and advised GlacierAI to schedule validation sweeps outside peak business hours. Throughput returned to baseline during the test window.
2) Medium-term (in progress): Autoscaler PR #88 updates the attach counting heuristic to exclude attachments with low recent token emission rate from healthy capacity calculations (merged to canary on 2026-03-13).
3) Medium-term (in progress): Serving runtime PR #621 makes checkpoint writer non-blocking and adds configurable IO backoff; rollout started on canary pool 2026-03-14.
4) Customer recommendations: limit concurrent long-lived validation streams to <=8 per worker during business hours, enable sidecar checkpoint backoff, and set per-tenant affinity caps in dedicated pool config.
5) Follow-up items: monitor attach_success_rate and slot-utilization for 72h post-rollout; SRE to re-evaluate SLA impact after 2026-03-17.

Status: partial mitigation achieved; engineering patches are rolling to canary and scheduled for production rollouts pending canary telemetry.
